source.title: Georgia EPD certified commercial laboratories for chemical and microbiological monitoring (revised January 9, 2025) + DPH/UGA Extension private-well guidance
limitations: Table lists in-state laboratories that appear on Georgia EPD’s Commercial Laboratories Certified for Microbiological Monitoring and/or Laboratories Certified for Chemical Monitoring PDFs (both revised January 9, 2025).
Georgia Environmental Protection Division Laboratory (Norcross) appears on both PDFs as EPA Certified but is omitted from the homeowner table — no private-well acceptance verified for EPD’s own lab.
Out-of-state labs on either PDF are omitted; use the official EPD PDFs.
EPD chemical PDF footnote: not all labs are certified for all groups of chemicals — verify analytes when you call.

Neither EPD roster labels private-well acceptance for commercial labs. Only UGA AESL is independently verified for private-well chemical testing via county Extension (W33C). County Environmental Health may offer bacterial testing — confirm locally.
Mail vs drop-off and prices intentionally omitted except Extension drop-off noted for UGA AESL.
Eurofins Atlanta street number differs between the two PDFs; both printed addresses are shown.

verified_paths.name: UGA AESL Private Well Chemical Test (W33C) via county Cooperative Extension
verified_paths.notes: DPH recommends W33C chemical screening about every 3 years for private wells; available through UGA county Extension offices. AESL Feed and Environmental Water Laboratory phone on EPD micro list and AESL forms: (706) 542-5350.

verified_paths.name: County Environmental Health bacterial testing (when offered)
verified_paths.notes: DPH recommends annual total/fecal coliform testing and states this may be available through the local County Environmental Health office. Confirm current services with your county office.
